_about: Curated Ark-SA signals. DATA, not code: the daily automation researches and updates this file (news-methodology: ≥3 independent sources per change), then runs scripts/ark_sa_daily_monitor.py. Every signal carries as_of; anything older than stale_after_days is reported as STALE with LOW confidence, and any reason or action with an `until` date in the past is dropped. The monitor never invents a current state it did not read.

signals.name: electricity_grid
signals.summary: National grid stable: Eskom reports 406+ consecutive days without load shedding (as of 26–27 Jun 2026). Localised load reduction continues in some high-risk feeders.
sources: IOL reporting on winter grid stability

reasons.text: National electricity grid stable (406+ days no load shedding) — positive offset.

signals.name: municipal_water
signals.summary: Bloemfontein/Mangaung water network under strain: vandalism on bulk pipelines, recurring outages in southern areas, and a planned 36-hour maintenance shutdown on 23–24 Jun. Supply restoration ongoing but fragile.

reasons.text: Bloemfontein/Mangaung water supply disrupted by vandalism, ageing pipes, and planned maintenance outages.

actions.text: Fill drinking-water containers and check household filters.

signals.name: fuel_supply
signals.summary: National fuel supply reported stable by DMPR and Fuel Retailers Association. March–April saw localised dry pumps from panic buying; July 2026 price decreases expected as oil eases and rand strengthens (~R16.50/USD).
sources: Central Energy Fund projections via AutoTrader/IOL

reasons.text: Food inflation easing and expected July fuel price decreases — positive offset.

actions.text: Top up vehicle fuel and keep cash plus a backup card/payment method.

signals.name: food_supply
signals.summary: Consumer food price inflation slowed to 1.6% (May 2026) with record grain harvest. El Niño developing — elevated drought risk for 2026/27 planting season; foot-and-mouth noted regionally.
sources: Stats SA via Daily Maverick analysis

signals.name: civil_unrest
signals.summary: Nationwide anti-immigration demonstrations planned 30 Jun 2026. Recent Free State looting: 140+ arrests in Mangaung (Bloemfontein/Botshabelo) and 15+ spaza shops looted in Thembalihle (17 Jun). Government says no indication of widespread unrest yet; R600m security deployment underway.
sources: SAnews.gov.za / IOL (30 Jun declared normal working day)
TimesLIVE / DefenceWeb on Free State arrests

reasons.text: Nationwide anti-immigration protests scheduled 30 Jun 2026 with major SAPS deployment (R600m).
Recent looting in Mangaung (Bloemfontein metro) and Thembalihle, Free State — situation contained but tension persists.

actions.text: Avoid non-essential travel through protest hotspots on 30 Jun; monitor SAPS/WC Gov road feeds if driving to Mossel Bay.
Secure home: lock gates, park vehicles off-street where possible during protest week.
If unrest spreads near Bloemfontein, limit movement to daylight hours on main roads only.

signals.name: banking_payments
signals.summary: No national banking outage. Isolated, resolved gateway degradations in June (Standard Bank Pay By Bank ~7h, PayU 3DSecure, Payfast ~1h).
sources: IsDown incident logs for PayU/Payfast/Standard Bank

signals.name: health_disease
signals.summary: Southern Africa cholera surge in neighbours (Mozambique, Zambia, Malawi); South Africa on alert after Feb floods damaged WASH infrastructure but no confirmed widespread SA cholera outbreak on health.gov.za tracker.
sources: ReliefWeb / Save the Children flood health note
National Department of Health cholera info page

reasons.text: Southern Africa cholera surge in neighbours; SA on alert but no confirmed widespread local outbreak.

actions.text: Refresh medicine stocks and charge power banks / two-way radios.

signals.name: weather_hazards
signals.summary: Garden Route severe flooding early Jun (200mm rain, fatalities, many district roads closed). As of 27 Jun, George/Knysna forecast mild/partly cloudy with 0% rain; new Yellow L4 rain warning for Cape Town/Winelands from 29 Jun.
sources: Garden Route District Municipality MACC updates
George Herald / Western Cape Government road bulletins

signals.name: global_shocks
signals.summary: Oil retreated to ~$73–80/bbl Brent after Middle East ceasefire framework; rand ~R16.50/USD. Venezuela M7.5 earthquake (24 Jun) — no direct SA impact.

signals.name: route_mobility
signals.summary: Primary N1/N2 corridors Bloemfontein→Garden Route generally passable. ~70% of storm-damaged WC roads reopened (22 Jun); many scenic/secondary routes still closed (Meiringspoort, Swartberg Pass, Seven Passes sections, etc.). Verify WC Government/SANRAL status before departure; avoid closed passes.
sources: IOL / Western Cape disaster recovery update (22 Jun)
George Herald / Western Cape Government road bulletins (18 Jun)

reasons.text: Garden Route secondary roads still closed after early-June flood damage; primary highways need pre-trip verification.

actions.text: Re-check route status via Western Cape Government and SANRAL before any Garden Route departure.

signals.name: family_readiness
signals.summary: Elevated readiness warranted: top up drinking water (local outages), fuel tanks, medicines, cash/backup payment options, comms charge, and paper maps. Caravan/move planning not urgent unless unrest escalates.
sources: Ark-SA readiness checklist (derived from local signals above)
